previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, obstructive sleep apnea, epilepsy, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for worsening left lower extremity swelling and erythema. She had recently completed a course of antibiotics but symptoms recurred, prompting admission. IV clindamycin and aztreonam were started, then switched to IV vancomycin after consultation with Infectious Disease, given partial response and concern for resistant organisms. The infection improved over five days, and she was transitioned back to oral doxycycline. During the stay, she experienced a brief absence-type seizure with left upper extremity tremors, evaluated by Neurology, who recommended continuing her current antiepileptic regimen with outpatient follow-up. Her chronic pain was managed with oxycodone and morphine, and diuretics were optimized for lymphedema. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline medications including warfarin, with plans for home IV diuretic therapy, neurology follow-up, and avoidance of topical steroids on the legs.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for an infection (cellulitis) in your legs, 
and increased fluid / swelling in your body. You were treated 
with IV lasix and IV antibiotics. Your symptoms improved with 
this treatment. You were transitioned to oral antibiotics 
(clindamycin) and your cellulitis continued to improve and fully 
resolved prior to discharge.  You were also transitioned back to 
oral diuretics (bumex), but finding an optimal oral diuretic 
regimen proved challenging, and is likely still a work in 
progress.  It is important that you do the following:

1) Weigh yourself on your home scale when you arrive home from 
the hospital and write that number down.

2) Weigh yourself each day, in the morning when you wake up 
(after you urinate, but before you eat or drink anything)

3) If your weight is more than 2 kilograms (4 lbs) more than the 
first recorded weight (from step 1), then you should notify your 
doctor and get IV ___ from the visiting nurse.

4) You should maintain a 1.5 - 2L fluid restriction per day 
(this includes water, juice, coffee, tea, soda, milk and any 
other beverages, as well as water or broth-based soups)

5) You should closely monitor the amount of sodium you consume 
on a daily basis (read all labels on food and drinks you 
consume).  You should limit your sodium intake to no more than 
___ mg (2 grams) per day.  This may be challenging, but 
excessive sodium intake can be a prime contributor to your fluid 
retention and leg swelling.

Please follow up with your primary care physician, ___ 
in the next ___ weeks to have your labs checked and to ensure 
that your diuretic regimen is still working well.  At that 
appointment, you can also discuss changing the antibiotic you 
take to prevent cellulitis (currently it is Doxycycline).
